minutes.headline: Commission approved solar panels at 116 Lancaster Street unanimously and will review its guidelines for solar policy.
minutes.summary: The Architectural Preservation District Commission met remotely, approved prior minutes, and discussed the old primary school's reuse, Brooks House, missing district signs and a possible operating budget. It proposed an annual endangered-properties list. It approved a certificate to alter 116 Lancaster Street for rooftop solar and agreed to revisit its guidelines on solar before the next meeting.

votes.motion: Approve the minutes of the January 20, 2021 meeting (roll call).
votes.outcome: passed (all four members aye by roll call; accepted as presented)

votes.motion: Accept the certificate to alter application for 116 Lancaster Street for rooftop solar panels.

votes.outcome: passed (all four members aye by roll call)

budget_items.what_was_said: A member asked for a letter to the town manager to find out the asking price in the RFP for the primary school, as the commission was not involved.
Members noted the commission has no budget and agreed to request an operating budget in the letter to the town manager, with a figure and spending ideas in mind.
A member said the Historical Commission has a small budget and the APDC should have at least that much.
Members discussed CPA, historic tax credits and housing authority grants; one member has found no responses so far and is seeking large grants.
A member cited a Ledger story on preliminary renovation costs being well over budget and wondered if that revives the idea of using the primary school as town hall.

decisions.decision: Member to send a letter to the town manager reminding that certificates to alter are required for Ritter and town hall repairs, copying the building inspector.
Colin Dwyer volunteered to contact Katie Adams about her earlier town campus idea.
Colin Dwyer to review prior minutes for the planning board's stated impediments to reusing Brooks House.
Letter to the town manager to ask what the primary school RFP asking price was.
Letter to the town manager will request an operating budget for the APDC, with examples of uses.
Members will review their guidelines on solar panels and discuss a policy at the next meeting.
Next meeting set for Wednesday March 24 at 7 pm.

what_happened.line: The commission voted 4-0 by roll call to accept the certificate to alter for rooftop solar panels at 116 Lancaster Street.
Members agreed to review their guidelines on solar panels and discuss a solar policy at the next meeting.
A letter to the town manager was agreed asking for an operating budget for the commission, which said it has none.

The letter will also ask what the asking price was in the old primary school RFP, since the commission was not involved, and remind the town that certificates to alter are required for Ritter and town hall repairs.
Next meeting was set for Wednesday March 24 at 7 pm.

why_it_matters: Approval of rooftop solar in a historic district, and a coming solar policy, shape what homeowners there can do to their roofs and how a certificate to alter is judged.
The commission has no operating budget and wants one; any amount would be a small line the town would have to fund, probably through taxes.
The questions about the primary school's reuse and RFP price, and about repairs to town buildings, touch how the town decides the future of public buildings.
